[RTR 19950905] suggests that same action includes "same, inherent
cardless action" anyway, using similar text to the NRA rule. (But not
being the NRA rule.)

And so far as I can tell, a bleed is a bleed is a bleed.

With [RTR 19950905] and [LSJ 20001122], it does tend to suggest that
these two things of "same action" tend to fade towards NRA's definitions
anyway.

>> >was canceled.

>>

>> terminated". [LSJ 20011204]
>> <3C0D0D63...@white-wolf.com>
>>
>> Action finished, so you hand it back, so far as I can tell.
>
>Could be, but there is a precedent with Force of Will/Change of Target\
>that indicates otherwise.

Force of Will states:

"Damage occurs after the action or combat is resolved."

There is no combat to resolve, because of Change of Target. And the
action doesn't resolve. Fine.

The action doesn't resolve - because it is irrevocably terminated ([LSJ
20011204]). This is also fine.

(That is, I'm reading it as "Damage occurs after the action is resolved
or after the combat is resolved" - which seems perfectly consistent with
card text.)

However, Spirit Marionette refers to the "end of the next action". An
action which is irrevocably terminated would seem to end. So it seems
to me that using Change of Target vs Force of Will as a template for a
ruling isn't necessary, because they don't work using the same
mechanics.

Or possibly: A minion cannot play the same action card more than once

than once each turn.

I'm unconvinced. Do there really exist groups who teach
new players the rules *without* NRA because it's too
complicated for them to learn right off the bat? Every
new player I've ever taught (or seen taught) the game,
it was taught to them with NRA in effect at all times.

I've also seen some evidence that learning to play at
tournaments is *not* that much different (in the sense
of being harder) from learning to play in general, eg
new players who win tournaments within a few months of
learning the game.

I haven't found the rule any harder to teach than the
rest of the game rules. Not repeating actions is a
pretty straightforward concept. The implementation
takes some explaining and some examples to become clear,
but that's no different from plenty of other things
about the game (eg aggravated damage or the definition
of a "hand strike").

>I'm using it to refer to a patch-fix that is almost painful in its
>patch-fix-ness.
>
>Not sure exactly what you're using the term as, after that rescue
>costing statement.

With the Archbishop and Prince, and Paralyze (by extension), situation
too, there have been a number of rules that have been done away
with/altered where the necessary set-up and explanation and
confusingness was quite a lot.

However, had they been *necessary* rules, we wouldn't have changed them.
One might see the current "One PA, including the card used to call the
vote per referendum" rule as a half-way house - an overlaid fix
(arguably derived from the original rules, but one which has been
through several modifications before being used, thus meaning later
expansions weren't designed with it in mind, IYSWIM) which isn't *that*
complicated, but is mildly difficult and annoying to explain to people.

In essence, the game has been stream-lined at a few points, except where
necessary bulk provides balance.

My emphasis is on the latter point. It is clear, from things like the
Gangrel Infinite Loop deck and cohorts, that the basic game - without a
restriction of the nature of NRA (but not necessarily NRA e.g. social
pressure can work similarly well in small, relatively controlled group
environments) - has a significant balance problem.

Hence I prefer kludginess (a painful, but necessary, solution) to
brokenness.

Suggestion: Potentially change the application time to "attempt", rather
than the resolution. This has interesting interactions with Mask etc.,
of course. (I've used "attempted" throughout below, where appropriate.
Change as necessary.)

Suggestion: Get rid of "types". Just say what you can and can't do in
plain English.

In most instances, a vampire will only be able to take an action once
per turn. Some effects, however, can untap them or otherwise allow them
to take an extra action. (e.g. Alexandra, Rutor's Hand, Force of Will)

1) Each of the actions in this rulebook can only be attempted once PER
TURN by a minion - that is, bleed, vote, ally... - whether you use a
card to provide the action or just use a "default" action. (e.g. you
can't bleed twice in a turn with the same minion, even if one action is
with Computer Hacking and the other is with the built-in bleed or a
different bleed action card entirely)

2) A minion cannot attempt actions using the same named card more than
once PER TURN. e.g. one minion cannot attempt Bum's Rush twice; you
cannot use Rayzeel's Song twice, even if you use it at two different
levels; Beast cannot attempt his built in rush more than once per turn.

That seems fairly painless to me - the bulk of the text being made up
from "e.g."

However, it does alter the state of play with regards Haven Uncovered,
Army of Rats et al.

Is that a bad thing? I'm unsure.

Wounded is possibly the most excellent thing in the world for describing
it.

Two vampires start combat with one another. They're both un-wounded.
If a vampire takes so much normal damage that he runs out of blood for
healing and then some more, he's wounded.
The first point of aggravated damage an un-wounded vampire takes wounds
him.
Any points of aggravated damage an already wounded vampire takes make
him burn a blood to prevent destruction for each one. (This isn't the
same as healing normal damage, but it can look like it, except for the
first point of aggravated damage to an un-wounded vampire, for which he
burns no blood.)

Wounded vampires go to torpor, and a vampire already in torpor is
wounded.

Not a lot else to be said.
